key_drivers: Five of the six prints since the Feb-2025 re-IPO closed down: 2026-06-09 -11.5%, 2026-03-18 -15.2%, 2025-12-09 -1.9%, 2025-09-09 -7.7%, 2025-06-11 +14.7%, 2025-03-26 -1.2% (close-to-close, Yahoo daily bars against SEC 8-K item 2.02 release timestamps). The one up print is the oldest.

The mechanism behind that run is repeatable and still in place: SailPoint beats on revenue and ARR and then guides margin/EPS at or below consensus. Q1 FY27 (2026-06-09) did exactly that - revenue +22% to $280M above the $276M consensus, ARR $1.163B +26% - and the stock fell 11.5% on a Q2 EPS guide of $0.07-0.08 whose $0.075 midpoint sat under the $0.08 consensus.
ARR growth is decelerating against a growth multiple: 26% reported in Q1, 24% implied by the company's own Q2 ARR guide of $1.218-1.222B. Decelerating ARR is the single number this stock trades on.

The bar for tomorrow is the company's own guide: revenue $308-312M, ARR $1.218-1.222B, EPS $0.07-0.08 against a $0.08 Nasdaq calendar consensus. Meeting it is not obviously enough - the last two quarters met it and sold off.

Against the call: the stock has already given back 21.9% from its 52-week high and fell 10.3% in the five sessions into the print, so some of this is priced; and it is still +75.9% off the 52-week low, which is a base that has held.
what_would_change_my_mind: A Q3 ARR guide implying re-acceleration rather than a third consecutive step down, or any sign the margin guide has stopped being set below consensus.
reasoning: The clearest repeated pattern on the board. Five of six prints down, and not as a coincidence - the cause is visible in each one. SailPoint delivers the top line and then hands the market a margin guide the market does not want, and the stock at a growth multiple cannot absorb a fourth consecutive quarter of ARR deceleration. Tomorrow's bar is the company's own Q2 guide, which is exactly what it met in June before falling 11.5%. The counter-argument is real and is why this is Lean rather than Strong: the stock is 22% off its high and down 10% in the week into the print, so the setup is de-risked in a way that June's was not. Magnitude is the more confident half of the call - median absolute move 9.6% over six prints, 20-day realised vol 71% annualised. Today's macro tape (strong jobs print, September rate-hike expectations, mega-cap tech down 2%) is a headwind for a high-multiple software name rather than a help. I do not have the option-implied move; it is marked unavailable rather than guessed.

key_drivers: Six of the last eight prints closed up: 2026-06-10 +20.3%, 2026-03-10 +3.8%, 2025-12-10 -5.3%, 2025-09-09 +3.8%, 2025-06-10 +11.6%, 2025-03-12 +6.2%, 2024-12-10 -0.3%, 2024-09-05 +7.4% (Yahoo daily bars keyed to SEC 8-K item 2.02 release times). Both prior Q1/September prints were up, +3.8% and +7.4%.

The stock has de-risked hard into the print with no company-specific catalyst found: -13.1% over 20 sessions, -19.0% from the 52-week high, and a multi-day losing streak through late August that contemporaneous coverage attributes to profit-taking and pre-earnings positioning after a +46.8% twelve-month run rather than to news.

The business is executing at the top of its range. FY26 closed with diluted EPS +31% to $19.16 and EBITDA up 23% to nearly $1.5B; Q4 alone printed EPS +66.2% and inside same-store sales +5.5% at a 42.4% inside margin.

FY27 guidance set in June - EBITDA +8-10%, inside same-store sales +2-5%, inside margin above 42%, at least 120 new stores - is the bar, and Q1 is the first quarter measured against it. Consensus for the quarter is $6.60 (Nasdaq calendar) to $6.78 (sell-side aggregate); I could not reconcile the two and have not picked one.

Against the call: Q1 covers the May-July peak-travel quarter, so retail fuel margin is the swing factor and I have no fuel-margin datum for that window - it is the reason this is Lean and not Strong. The stock also still trades at a demanding multiple on a 46% twelve-month gain.
what_would_change_my_mind: A soft retail fuel margin in the May-July window, or any trim to the FY27 EBITDA growth range set in June.
reasoning: A company compounding at the top of its own guidance, whose stock has fallen 13% in twenty sessions into the print on what the available coverage describes as positioning rather than news, with a reaction history that is six-up-of-eight and two-for-two on this specific quarter. That combination is the closest thing to a directional edge I can find on the long side today. The reason it is Lean and not Strong is that Casey's Q1 is the fuel-margin quarter and I have no anchor for May-July retail fuel margins; a weak one has produced the down prints in this series before. Magnitude: median absolute move around 5% across the eight, but the distribution has a fat right tail - +20.3% in June, +11.6% the June before - and 20-day realised vol is 32.5% annualised. I have set 5.5% rather than the 3.8% the median-of-eight proxy would give, because that proxy is dragged down by three near-zero prints and the recent quarters have been much larger. Option-implied move unavailable.

company: Sunbelt Rentals Holdings, Inc. (NYSE/LSE dual line; formerly Ashtead Group, US primary listing since Feb 2026)
key_drivers: Both prints since the US listing closed down: 2026-06-23 -9.4% and 2026-03-12 -1.9% (Yahoo daily bars keyed to SEC 8-K item 2.02 timestamps). Only two events - this is a thin base rate and is treated as such.

Two sell-side price-target cuts landed in the week before the print, both from negative ratings: JPMorgan to $71 from $74 on 2026-09-01 with an Underweight, and Bank of America to $62 from $65 with an Underperform. The stock closed 2026-09-04 at $68.59, so the BofA target sits roughly 10% below spot.

The unresolved issue is margin, not revenue. FY26 Q4 grew rental revenue about 8% to total revenue of $2,754M with adjusted EBITDA of $1,067M at a 38.7% margin, but margin fell roughly 290bps, and the FY27 guide - total revenue +4.5-7.5%, rental revenue +5-8%, adjusted EBITDA $4.85-5.05B - implies margins broadly flat rather than recovering. Q1 is the first quarter tested against it.

Macro runs against an equipment-rental cyclical today: an unexpectedly strong jobs report has pushed expectations toward a September rate hike with Treasury yields higher, which is a direct headwind to the non-residential construction demand this company rents into.

Against the call, and the reason evidence quality is low: the tape into this print is contaminated. Volume ran 13.2M on 2026-08-28 and 28.4M on 2026-08-31 against a ~6.3M twenty-day average, followed by -7.2% on 2026-09-01. That signature is an index-flow event, not information. I could not confirm which index event it was, so the -12.2% twenty-day drawdown cannot be read cleanly as informed selling.
what_would_change_my_mind: Any evidence of rental-rate or margin recovery in the Q1 print, or confirmation that the late-August drawdown was entirely mechanical index flow rather than positioning.
reasoning: Three independent negatives point the same way: both prints since the US listing were down, two negative-rated houses cut targets in the week before this one with BofA now roughly 10% under spot, and the margin question the June guide left open gets its first test tomorrow into a tape that has just repriced toward a rate hike. That is enough for a lean and not more. The reason confidence is low is the tape itself - 28 million shares on 2026-08-31 against a 6.3 million average is an index event, and I could not establish which one, so I cannot tell how much of the 12% twenty-day drawdown is information and how much is mechanics. A two-event base rate compounds that. Magnitude 6.5%: the two prior prints were 9.4% and 1.9%, 20-day realised vol is 42% annualised, and a first-quarter test of a contested margin guide is the kind of print that moves. Option-implied move unavailable.

key_drivers: This specific quarter has been the disaster quarter two years running: 2025-09-09 -25.4% and 2024-09-04 -15.8%. It is the print where a full construction season of data forces the fiscal-year reset, and twice the reset was a cut. Full history: 2026-06-10 -6.1%, 2026-03-24 +4.5%, 2025-12-09 +2.1%, 2025-09-09 -25.4%, 2025-06-10 -2.1%, 2025-03-25 -0.2%, 2024-12-03 +15.5%, 2024-09-04 -15.8%.

But the asymmetry has inverted. Going into the 2025-09-09 air pocket the stock was at $66.59 near its highs; it is now $43.69, down 34.8% over twelve months and only 3.9% above the 52-week low. The market is already positioned for the cut that ambushed it twice.

The FY26 guide reaffirmed in June - net sales $7.8-7.9B, adjusted EBITDA $950-980M, cash conversion 60-70%, end-market volumes roughly flat - is what gets reset tomorrow, and Q1 already disappointed against it (2026-06-10 -6.1% on $1.91B sales and $0.72 adjusted EPS).

The demand commentary is genuinely constructive: municipal demand strong and roughly 95% state/local funded, highway and street strong, institutional steady, and data-centre volumes growing off a small base. Consensus for the quarter is $0.91 (Nasdaq calendar) to $0.92 on about $2.14B, which is only about 2.4% revenue growth - a low bar.
Rate-hike expectations after today's jobs report are a headwind to the residential and non-residential construction mix, though the municipal majority insulates a lot of it.
what_would_change_my_mind: Confirmation either way on the FY26 EBITDA range - a cut, or a reaffirmation with Q2 organic volume growth intact - would resolve this into a directional call immediately.
reasoning: Two forces of similar size point opposite ways and I cannot separate them. The seasonal record says this is the print where Core & Main resets the year and gets destroyed for it - minus 25.4% and minus 15.8% in the last two Septembers, which is a mechanism rather than a coincidence. Against that, the setup is nothing like either of those years: the stock is 34.8% lower over twelve months and sits 3.9% off its 52-week low, so the cut those years came as a surprise is now most of what is in the price, and the quarter's own bar is only about 2.4% revenue growth. Abstaining is the honest output. What I will commit to is size: this is the highest-variance name in the window after SAIL. The eight-print median absolute move is 5.3% but the mean is 9.0%, and the tails cluster precisely in September. 8.5% raw is a deliberate step above the median proxy because the median understates a distribution this fat-tailed, which the backtest showed is the recurring error. Option-implied move unavailable.

key_drivers: The reaction history splits almost evenly and, more importantly, it fades: 2026-06-05 +4.1% on a +11.7% gap, 2026-03-12 -3.6%, 2025-12-05 +10.5%, 2025-09-05 +13.6% on a +11.8% gap, 2025-06-06 -6.9% on a -12.6% gap, 2025-03-13 -3.7%, 2025-01-14 -3.9%. Three up, four down close-to-close, but the opening gaps are routinely 12% and give much of it back.
The one directly comparable quarter - Q2 FY27 against Q2 FY26 on 2025-09-04 - was +13.6%. One observation.

The stock has fallen 14.2% in five sessions into the print with no company news I could find, after spiking +9.1% on 2026-08-27 alongside SAIL's +12.2% the same day, which reads as a sector move given and then taken back rather than anything specific to ServiceTitan. Insider selling is on the tape: the CFO sold 9,000 shares for $817,500 on 2026-08-29, part of roughly -$2.28M net insider selling over 90 days, all executives.

Fundamental momentum is the other way. Q1 FY27 beat on revenue and EPS, revenue $268.8M +25%, net loss narrowed 51% to $22.8M, and the full-year outlook was raised; the shares jumped 14% after hours before fading to +4.1%.

Consensus is ambiguous in the sources I have - the Nasdaq calendar carries ($0.09) and a sell-side aggregate carries $0.26, which is a GAAP-versus-adjusted gap I could not resolve. Analyst consensus target is $110.4 against an $84 spot.
what_would_change_my_mind: Any explanation for the 14% five-session slide - a pre-announcement, a peer read-across, a downgrade - would turn a coin flip into a call in whichever direction it pointed.
reasoning: A company that has beaten and raised every quarter as a public company, whose stock has fallen 14% in five sessions into the print for no reason I can find, with executives selling into the slide. Those two readings - de-risked setup primed for a relief rally, versus informed positioning ahead of a stumble - are equally available and I have nothing that discriminates between them. The 08-27 spike and give-back mirrors SAIL almost exactly, which suggests factor rather than fundamentals and further weakens the price signal. Neutral is the answer, and the backtest's own record says a Neutral here is worth more than a guess. Size is the part I will stand behind: opening gaps on this name have run 12% in three of seven prints, 20-day realised vol is 56.6% annualised, and the shares are 29.7% off the 52-week high while still 52.1% above the low - a wide, unresolved range. The close-to-close median of 4.1% badly understates that, so I have set 9.0%. Option-implied move unavailable.

key_drivers: Reaction history is violent and two-sided: 2026-06-10 -2.1%, 2026-03-25 +13.3%, 2025-12-10 +1.5%, 2025-09-10 -16.6%, 2025-06-11 -11.0%, 2025-03-26 -1.1%, 2024-12-04 -0.5%, 2024-08-28 +11.1%. Three up, five down, median absolute move 6.5%, but four of the eight were larger than 10%.

The bad news is already on the table. In June, Chewy cut FY26 net sales guidance to $13.40-13.55B citing a consumer pet environment that had become incrementally more challenged, and said quarterly active-customer adds would trend toward the low end of the 150,000-250,000 range. The stock fell only 2.1% on that, which says the cut was expected.

It is also already washed out: $22.92, down 45.8% over twelve months and 45.5% below the 52-week high, though up 13.8% over three months off the lows. Sell-side is split - Morgan Stanley cut its target to $37 from $42 on 2026-08-21, Raymond James raised to $28 from $25.

What Chewy held in June was the profitability line - FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance kept at 6.6-6.8%, about 100bps of expansion at the midpoint. That, not sales, is the number the print will be judged on, and I have no read on whether it survives a second soft quarter.

The September print is the one that has hurt twice before, -16.6% in 2025 and a -11.0% June ahead of it, both when the stock was materially higher; the same disappointment from $22.92 is a different trade.
what_would_change_my_mind: Whether the 6.6-6.8% FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guide is held or cut - that single line decides this print, and I have no advance read on it.
reasoning: Chewy already told the market the year was getting worse - in June, and the stock took it with a 2% shrug. That is the single most important fact here and it cuts the legs off a directional call in either direction: the pessimism is largely in the price at $22.92 after a 46% twelve-month decline, but a second cut from a company that has now cut once would still hurt. The print turns on one line, the 6.6-6.8% FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guide, and I have no advance read on it. Guessing the sign of a coin I cannot see is exactly what the abstention rule exists for. On size I am more confident: half of the last eight prints exceeded 10% and this is a name that gaps 9-12% routinely, so 8.0% rather than the 6.5% median. I have also not tried to reconcile the $0.33 sell-side and $0.18 Nasdaq-calendar EPS figures for the quarter - they are almost certainly adjusted versus GAAP, but I have not confirmed that and so have not used either as a bar.

company: Jersey Mike's Subs Inc. (Class A; IPO 2026-07-30 at $23.00)
key_drivers: There is no reaction history at all. EDGAR carries no prior 8-K item 2.02 for CIK 0002127043 and the price series is 28 sessions long. This is the company's first earnings report as a public company, so every base rate the other seven names have is simply absent here.

It priced 43,478,261 Class A shares at $23.00 on 2026-07-29 and began trading 2026-07-30; it closed 2026-09-08 around $21.33, roughly 7% below the IPO price. Trading below issue into a first print is a mild negative, but on 28 sessions it is close to noise.

The stock is already volatile without any earnings: daily moves of +6.4%, +6.3%, -5.6%, +5.3%, +5.1% and -4.8% inside its first month, on a 52-week range of $19.86-$24.99 that is really just a one-month range.

Sell-side initiated after the quiet period expired - Tigress, Goldman Sachs, Bernstein, BTIG and William Blair, with targets clustered $26-29, all above the current price. Nasdaq consensus for the quarter is $0.23.

The real content of a first print is the first company-issued forward guide, which by definition has no history to be measured against, and the S-1 numbers are only weeks old so a large miss on the quarter itself is unlikely.
what_would_change_my_mind: Nothing available before the print. This becomes forecastable only once there is a guide and one reaction to compare against.
reasoning: A first earnings report six weeks after an IPO, with zero reaction history, no prior guide to be measured against, and a price series too short to characterise. There is no basis for a directional call and I am not going to manufacture one from the fact that it trades 7% below issue - on 28 sessions that is noise. Neutral here is not a failure to produce an answer, it is the answer. Magnitude is the one thing the short record does support: a stock that has printed six daily moves above 4.5% in its first month without an earnings catalyst will not print a quiet first result, and first post-IPO reports are among the highest-variance events there are, since the forward guide arrives with no anchor. 9.0% is a judgement, not an extrapolation from a base rate, and evidence quality is scored at 30 to say so. I have deliberately not used the $26-29 initiation targets as a signal; those were published inside the coverage-initiation window and say more about underwriter syndicate composition than about tomorrow.

key_drivers: Korn Ferry guides the quarter it is about to report, which removes most of the surprise from the quarter itself: it told the market to expect fee revenue of $725-745M and diluted EPS of $1.32-1.38, and the Nasdaq calendar consensus is $1.35, sitting on the midpoint. The move therefore comes from the Q2 guide and new-business trends, neither of which I have a read on.

The reaction history leans up but not decisively: 2026-06-23 +5.8%, 2026-03-09 -1.5%, 2025-12-09 +4.0%, 2025-09-09 +0.6%, 2025-06-18 +6.5%, 2025-03-11 +7.6%, 2024-12-05 -8.4%, 2024-09-05 -4.7%. Five up, three down, median absolute move about 5.2%. The two September prints in that set are the weakest pair, +0.6% and -4.7%.

The setup is the opposite of de-risked: the stock is only 5.3% below its 52-week high and 37.2% above the low, up 30.5% over six months, so the bar is a high one. It fell 4.2% today, the session before the print, which is a partial-day observation and I have not established a cause.

This quarter introduces a reporting-structure change from solution-based to regional segments (Americas, EMEA, APAC), with new business, fee revenue and estimated remaining fees still shown across Search, Talent & Organizational Solutions, and Workforce Solutions. Re-cut segments make the print harder to read against models on the day and add reaction noise in a direction I cannot sign.
FY26 new business was $543.9M with 43% from new-logo clients. Workforce Solutions/RPO has been the soft end of this business and is the line most exposed if hiring cools.
what_would_change_my_mind: The Q2 FY27 guide relative to the $1.32-1.38 shape of this one, and whether RPO new business is growing - either would settle the call.
reasoning: Two things cancel. The base rate leans up, five of eight, and Korn Ferry has a habit of landing inside or above the guide it sets. But that same habit is why the quarter is nearly a non-event: the company pre-guided fee revenue and EPS, consensus sits on the midpoint, and the surprise has to come from the forward guide instead. Meanwhile the stock is 5.3% off its 52-week high after a 30.5% six-month run, which is the least forgiving setup on this board, and the two September prints in the history are the two weakest in it. Add a segment-reporting change that will make the print messy to read on the day and the sign is genuinely undetermined. This is also the lowest-variance name in the window and the only one I have put below 5%: 20-day realised vol is 22.7% annualised, the median print move is about 5.2% but three of the eight were under 2%, and pre-guiding compresses the quarter's own contribution. That keeps the raw estimate at 4.5% and, under the correction rule, leaves the scaled number unchanged.
